title: Module 2 · Vancomycin and Aminoglycoside Dosing
intro: Vancomycin AUC dosing with full worked math, loading doses, obesity, dialysis, continuous infusion, children, oral vancomycin, and aminoglycosides: dosing weight, Hartford, traditional levels, synergy and toxicity.

cases.title: Why vancomycin needs a pharmacist
cases.stem: A 62 year old man has MRSA in 2 of 2 blood cultures. The team orders "vancomycin per pharmacy." This is the first time you dose it alone.

steps.q: What does vancomycin exposure need to reach for serious MRSA infection?

options.t: An AUC over 24 hours of 400 to 600 (assuming MIC 1)
options.why: The 2020 consensus guideline target for serious MRSA infection (Rybak 2020, Recommendation 1).

options.t: A trough of 15 to 20 mcg/mL
options.why: Trough only dosing to 15 to 20 is no longer recommended: it overshoots AUC in many patients and raises kidney injury.

options.t: A peak above 40 mcg/mL
options.why: Vancomycin kill depends on total exposure over time, not on a high peak.

options.t: Any detectable level
options.why: Too low exposure risks treatment failure.

steps.teach: Vancomycin is **time and exposure dependent**. Think "area under the curve," the total drug the bug sees over a day, not one number at one moment.
steps.where: Rybak 2020 consensus guideline, Recommendation 1. St. Mary's pharmacy to dose policy tells you what software or method you use.

steps.q: What is the preferred way to estimate AUC?

options.t: Bayesian software using one or two levels
options.why: Preferred by the guideline: works with levels drawn at any time, even before steady state.

options.t: Two levels (a peak and a trough) with first order equations
options.why: An accepted alternative when Bayesian software is not available.

options.t: One trough only, compared to 15 to 20
options.why: This is the old method the guideline moved away from.

steps.q: When should the AUC target be reached?

options.t: Preferably within the first 24 to 48 hours
options.why: Early target attainment matters in serious infection (Rybak 2020, Recommendation 3).

options.t: Within a week
options.why: Too slow for bacteremia.

options.t: Only after the third day of therapy
options.why: Waiting for full steady state delays good exposure; Bayesian tools let you dose early.

cases.monitor: Serum creatinine at least daily early on, urine output, AUC estimate once and again if kidney function changes, blood cultures until negative.
cases.pearl: **Vanc target: AUC 400 to 600, early, by Bayesian or two levels. No more trough only to 15 to 20.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: The loading dose
cases.stem: An 80 kg woman in septic shock. CrCl about 35 mL/min and falling. The resident wants to "reduce the first dose because of her kidneys."

steps.q: Should the first (loading) dose be reduced for her kidney function?

options.t: No. The loading dose depends on body size (volume of distribution), not on kidney function
options.why: Kidney function decides how much and how often you give after the first dose. The load fills the "bucket."

options.t: Yes, cut it in half
options.why: An underdosed first dose leaves a septic patient without effective exposure for a day or more.

options.t: Skip the load and start maintenance
options.why: Critically ill patients are the ones who benefit most from a load.

steps.teach: **Load by weight, maintain by kidneys.** That one sentence prevents a very common error.

steps.q: What loading dose range does the guideline allow, and what maximum?

options.t: 20 to 35 mg/kg actual body weight, maximum 3,000 mg
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 10. For her, 20 to 25 mg/kg is 1,600 to 2,000 mg.

options.t: 10 mg/kg, maximum 1,000 mg
options.why: Too low for a load.

options.t: 50 mg/kg with no maximum
options.why: Above the guideline range; the cap is 3,000 mg.

steps.q: You choose 2,000 mg. By the FDA label rate (no faster than 10 mg/min), how long is the minimum infusion?

options.t: 200 minutes (about 3 hours 20 minutes)
options.why: 2,000 mg divided by 10 mg/min = 200 minutes. Many hospitals use a faster 1 g per hour policy; follow St. Mary's.

options.t: 60 minutes
options.why: Too fast for 2,000 mg by the label rate.

options.t: 20 minutes
options.why: Far too fast: high risk of vancomycin infusion reaction and hypotension.

steps.teach: Infusion time is a safety check you do on every vancomycin order. Fast infusion causes flushing, itching and low BP (infusion reaction, not a true allergy).
steps.where: Vancomycin label, Dosage and Administration. St. Mary's IV administration guide for the local rate.

cases.call: **S/B:** Septic shock, 80 kg, CrCl 35 and falling, vancomycin ordered. **A:** The loading dose should not be reduced for kidney function. **R:** I recommend 2,000 mg IV now (25 mg/kg), then I will choose the maintenance dose by kidney function and check levels in the first 24 to 48 hours.
cases.pearl: **Load by weight (20 to 35 mg/kg, max 3 g). Maintain by kidneys.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Empiric maintenance dose
cases.stem: A 58 year old man, 72 kg, SCr 1.0 mg/dL, normal and stable. MRSA osteomyelitis. You need a starting maintenance dose.

steps.q: Calculate his CrCl (Cockcroft Gault).

options.t: About 82 mL/min
About 41 mL/min
options.why: Check the formula: (140 minus age) x weight / (72 x SCr).

options.t: About 120 mL/min
options.why: Recheck the arithmetic.

steps.q: Which starting regimen fits the usual adult range (15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours)?

options.t: 1,250 mg IV every 12 hours (about 17 mg/kg)
options.why: Inside the guideline range for normal kidney function. Then confirm with levels.

options.t: 500 mg IV every 24 hours
options.why: Much too low for normal kidneys.

options.t: 2,500 mg IV every 8 hours
options.why: About 35 mg/kg every 8 hours: far above the range.

steps.q: When will you get levels?

options.t: Early, so an AUC estimate is available within 24 to 48 hours (often around the third or fourth dose with two levels, or sooner with Bayesian software)
options.why: Serious infection and a long course both call for AUC monitoring.

options.t: Never, because his kidneys are normal
options.why: Long, serious courses need monitoring even with normal kidneys.

cases.pearl: **15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours to start, then let the levels decide.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Calculating AUC with two levels
cases.stem: Vancomycin 1,000 mg IV every 12 hours, infused over 1 hour, at steady state. Peak drawn 1 hour after the end of the infusion (2 hours after the start): **30 mcg/mL**. Trough drawn 30 minutes before the next dose (11.5 hours after the start): **10 mcg/mL**.

steps.q: Step 1: calculate the elimination rate constant (ke).

options.t: ke = ln(30/10) / 9.5 h = about 0.116 per hour
options.why: Time between the two levels: 11.5 minus 2 = 9.5 hours. ln(3) = 1.099; 1.099 / 9.5 = 0.116 per hour.

options.t: ke = (30 minus 10) / 12 = 1.67 per hour
options.why: Elimination is exponential, so you need the natural log of the ratio, and the time between the actual draws.
That would assume a 12 hour half life; you calculate the half life from ke, not the reverse.

steps.teach: **ke = ln(C1 / C2) / time between the draws.** Half life = 0.693 / ke. Here half life is about 6 hours.

steps.q: Step 2: estimate the true peak at the end of the infusion (1 hour after the start).

options.t: About 33.7 mcg/mL (30 x e raised to 0.116 x 1)
options.why: Back extrapolate 1 hour: 30 x 1.123 = 33.7.

options.t: 30 mcg/mL
options.why: The drawn level is 1 hour after the end of the infusion; the true end of infusion peak is higher.

options.t: 60 mcg/mL
options.why: Too high: one hour of decay at this ke is only about 12%.

steps.q: Step 3: estimate the true trough at the end of the interval (12 hours).

options.t: About 9.4 mcg/mL (10 x e raised to minus 0.116 x 0.5)
options.why: Forward extrapolate 30 minutes: 10 x 0.944 = 9.4.

options.t: 10 mcg/mL
options.why: Close, but the draw was 30 minutes early.

steps.q: Step 4: calculate AUC for one dose, then AUC over 24 hours. Infusion part = infusion time x (Cmax + Cmin) / 2. Elimination part = (Cmax minus Cmin) / ke.

options.t: Infusion part 21.6 + elimination part 209.6 = 231 per dose; x 2 doses = AUC24 about 462
AUC24 about 231
options.why: That is one dose interval. Multiply by 24 / 12 = 2.

options.t: AUC24 about 960
options.why: Recheck the math; that would be well above the toxic range.

steps.q: AUC24 is about 462. What do you do?

options.t: Continue the current regimen and keep monitoring kidney function
options.why: 462 is inside 400 to 600.

options.t: Increase the dose because the trough is only 10
options.why: This is exactly the old trough thinking the guideline moved away from. The AUC is on target.

options.t: Decrease the dose
options.why: Not needed; the AUC is on target.

steps.teach: A trough of 10 can go with a perfect AUC. Pushing the trough to 15 to 20 would push this AUC far over 600.

cases.pearl: **ke = ln(C1/C2)/time. Extrapolate to true Cmax and Cmin. AUC = infusion part + elimination part, times doses per day.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Adjusting to the target
cases.stem: On vancomycin 1,000 mg every 12 hours, the Bayesian estimate is AUC24 = 320. Kidney function is stable. Goal AUC about 500.

steps.q: Vancomycin follows linear kinetics. What new total dose reaches about 500?

options.t: About 1,500 mg every 12 hours (1,000 x 500/320 = 1,560; round to 1,500, predicted AUC about 480)
options.why: Linear kinetics: AUC changes in proportion to the dose when the interval and kidney function stay the same.

options.t: 2,500 mg every 12 hours
options.why: That predicts an AUC near 800: toxic range.

options.t: Keep 1,000 mg and recheck in a week
options.why: An AUC of 320 is below target for a serious infection.

steps.teach: **New dose = old dose x (target AUC / current AUC).** Round to a measurable dose and recheck after the change.

steps.q: When do you recheck exposure after a dose change?

options.t: After the new regimen is close to steady state, or sooner with Bayesian software; and any time kidney function changes
options.why: Recheck is required when the dose or the kidneys change.

options.t: Never; one level is enough for the whole course
options.why: Kidney function changes during illness; exposure changes with it.

cases.pearl: **Linear: new dose = old dose x target / current.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Too much exposure
cases.stem: Day 5 of vancomycin and piperacillin tazobactam for a diabetic foot infection. SCr rose from 0.9 to 1.5 mg/dL. Estimated AUC24 is 780.

steps.q: What is happening?

options.t: Drug exposure is above 600 and kidney injury is starting
options.why: AUC above 600 is linked to higher risk of acute kidney injury.

options.t: This is expected and needs no change
options.why: A 67% rise in creatinine meets the definition of kidney injury.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Hold the next dose, recheck a level, and restart at a lower dose or longer interval guided by the new AUC
options.why: The fastest way to protect the kidneys is to stop more drug going in until the level falls.

options.t: Ask if MRSA is actually suspected or confirmed, and whether vancomycin is still needed
options.why: Stewardship: if cultures do not show MRSA, stopping vancomycin is the best kidney protection.

options.t: Ask whether piperacillin tazobactam could be changed (for example to cefepime) if coverage allows
options.why: Observational studies link vancomycin plus piperacillin tazobactam to more kidney injury; it is a reasonable question to raise.

options.t: Add furosemide to protect the kidneys
options.why: Loop diuretics do not protect the kidneys and can add to the problem.

steps.q: How strong is the evidence that piperacillin tazobactam increases vancomycin kidney injury?

options.t: Mostly observational; the guideline says it has been reported to raise the risk
options.why: Raise it as a risk, not as proven cause. Whether creatinine changes reflect true injury is still debated.

options.t: Proven by large randomized trials
options.why: The data are mostly observational.

cases.call: **S/B:** Day 5 vancomycin plus pip tazo, SCr 0.9 to 1.5, AUC 780. **A:** Exposure is above target and kidney injury is starting. **R:** I recommend holding tonight's dose, a level in the morning, and restarting at a lower dose. Do the cultures still support MRSA coverage? If not, can we stop vancomycin?
cases.pearl: **AUC above 600 + rising creatinine = hold, recheck, re dose, and ask if vanc is still needed.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Red man? Infusion reaction
cases.setting: Med surg · 30 minutes into an infusion
cases.stem: A nurse calls: "The vancomycin is running and my patient's face, neck and chest are bright red and itchy. BP 112/70, breathing fine, no wheeze."

steps.q: What is this most likely?

options.t: Vancomycin infusion reaction (histamine release from a fast infusion)
options.why: Rate related, not IgE mediated. Flushing of the upper body and itching are classic.

options.t: Anaphylaxis requiring permanent allergy listing
options.why: No hypotension, airway symptoms or wheeze. Listing it as an allergy wrongly can block a needed drug later.

steps.q: What do you tell the nurse?

options.t: Pause the infusion, give an antihistamine (for example diphenhydramine) if ordered, and restart at a slower rate once symptoms ease
options.why: Most patients tolerate the drug when infused more slowly.

options.t: Document it as an infusion reaction, not an allergy, and consider antihistamine before future doses with a longer infusion time
options.why: Accurate documentation protects the patient later.

options.t: Stop vancomycin forever and switch to daptomycin
options.why: Not needed for an infusion reaction.

cases.pearl: **Red and itchy, BP fine = too fast. Pause, antihistamine, slower.**

sources.t: Vancomycin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Vancomycin in obesity
cases.stem: A 41 year old woman, 160 kg, CrCl about 120 mL/min, MRSA bacteremia from a skin source.

steps.q: Which loading dose does the guideline suggest in obesity?

options.t: 20 to 25 mg/kg actual body weight, maximum 3,000 mg
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 12. 20 mg/kg x 160 kg = 3,200 mg, so the cap of 3,000 mg applies.

options.t: 25 mg/kg ideal body weight
options.why: Vancomycin loading uses actual body weight.

options.t: 35 mg/kg actual weight with no cap
options.why: That is 5,600 mg: far above the 3,000 mg cap.

steps.q: What is a usual ceiling for the empiric daily maintenance total in obese patients?

options.t: Usually not above 4,500 mg per day, depending on kidney function
options.why: Then let AUC monitoring guide changes.

options.t: No ceiling; give 20 mg/kg every 8 hours by actual weight (9,600 mg/day)
options.why: Clearance does not rise in proportion to weight. This overshoots badly.

cases.pearl: **Obese: load 20 to 25 mg/kg actual (max 3 g), maintenance usually 4.5 g/day or less, then AUC.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Vancomycin and hemodialysis
cases.stem: A 70 kg man on intermittent hemodialysis three times a week (high permeability dialyzer) has an MRSA line infection. Vancomycin is to be given after dialysis.

steps.q: What loading dose does the guideline list after dialysis?

options.t: 25 mg/kg (about 1,750 mg)
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 13: 25 mg/kg after dialysis ends, for either dialyzer type.

options.t: 5 mg/kg because the kidneys do not work
options.why: The load fills the volume of distribution regardless of kidney function.

steps.q: What maintenance dose follows, and how is it monitored?

options.t: About 10 mg/kg after each session (high permeability), with a pre dialysis level at least weekly; pre dialysis levels of 15 to 20 likely reach the AUC target
options.why: Dialysis removes vancomycin, so you redose after each session and check the level before dialysis.

options.t: A dose every day with daily troughs
options.why: Dosing is tied to the dialysis schedule.

cases.pearl: **HD: 25 mg/kg load, then about 10 mg/kg after each session (high flux); check pre dialysis levels.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Continuous infusion vancomycin
cases.stem: The ICU uses continuous infusion vancomycin for a 75 kg patient.

steps.q: What does the guideline suggest for loading and maintenance?

options.t: Load 15 to 20 mg/kg, then 30 to 40 mg/kg per day (up to 60) as a continuous infusion
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 7.

options.t: No load; 10 mg/kg per day
options.why: Too low.

steps.q: The steady state level is 22 mcg/mL. What is the AUC24?

options.t: About 528 (22 x 24)
options.why: With a continuous infusion, AUC24 = steady state concentration x 24. The guideline target level is 20 to 25.
Multiply by 24 hours.

steps.q: What line issue matters most with continuous vancomycin?

options.t: Y site compatibility with other drugs running in the same line, since it runs all day
options.why: Check Trissel's for every drug sharing the line, or give it a dedicated lumen.

options.t: None
options.why: A drug running 24 hours meets every other drug in that line.

cases.pearl: **Continuous vanc: AUC = level x 24. Target level 20 to 25.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Children and vancomycin
cases.stem: A 6 year old, 20 kg, normal kidney function, MRSA osteomyelitis.

steps.q: Which empiric total daily dose range does the guideline suggest for children 3 months and older?

options.t: 60 to 80 mg/kg per day divided every 6 to 8 hours
options.why: Children clear vancomycin faster than adults; older lower doses often underdose. Children under 12 often need the upper end.

options.t: 15 mg/kg once daily
options.why: Far too low for a child with normal kidneys.

steps.q: For 20 kg at 60 mg/kg/day every 6 hours, what is each dose?

options.t: 300 mg every 6 hours
options.why: 60 x 20 = 1,200 mg per day, divided by 4 = 300 mg.

options.t: 1,200 mg every 6 hours
options.why: That is the whole day's dose given four times.

steps.q: Which reference do you open for pediatric dosing?

options.t: A pediatric reference (Lexicomp Pediatric or Harriet Lane) and St. Mary's pediatric protocol
options.why: Never use the adult section for a child.

options.t: The adult Lexicomp monograph
options.why: Adult doses do not translate by weight alone.

cases.pearl: **Kids clear vanc fast: 60 to 80 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours, then AUC.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Oral vancomycin is a different drug
cases.stem: A patient has a first episode of C. difficile infection. The order reads "vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours."

steps.q: What is wrong?

options.t: IV vancomycin does not reach the colon; C. difficile needs oral vancomycin
options.why: Vancomycin is poorly absorbed from the gut and IV drug does not get into the colon lumen in useful amounts.

options.t: Nothing
options.why: IV vancomycin does not treat C. difficile colitis.

steps.q: What does the IDSA/SHEA 2021 update recommend for a first episode?

options.t: Fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily for 10 days preferred; oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily for 10 days is an acceptable alternative
options.why: Fidaxomicin is preferred because it lowers recurrence; vancomycin is the common alternative, often for cost or access.

options.t: Metronidazole 500 mg three times daily as first choice for everyone
options.why: Metronidazole is now only for nonsevere disease when the others are unavailable.

cases.call: **S/B:** First C. diff episode, IV vancomycin ordered. **A:** IV vancomycin does not reach the colon. **R:** Change to fidaxomicin 200 mg PO twice daily for 10 days, or vancomycin 125 mg PO four times daily for 10 days if fidaxomicin is not available.
cases.pearl: **C. diff = oral vancomycin (or fidaxomicin). IV vanc does nothing in the colon.**

sources.t: Johnson S, et al. IDSA/SHEA 2021 focused update: C. difficile infection in adults. Clin Infect Dis 2021;73:e1029-e1044

cases.title: How aminoglycosides kill
cases.stem: You are about to verify your first gentamicin order.

steps.q: What kind of killing do aminoglycosides show?

options.t: Concentration dependent killing with a post antibiotic effect
options.why: Higher peaks kill faster, and bacteria stay suppressed for hours after levels fall. That is why one large dose a day works.

options.t: Time dependent killing like beta lactams
options.why: That describes penicillins and cephalosporins.

steps.q: What are the main toxicities?

options.t: Kidney injury (usually reversible)
options.why: Watch creatinine and urine output.

options.t: Ototoxicity, hearing and balance (often irreversible)
options.why: Ask about ringing in the ears, hearing loss and dizziness.

options.t: Neuromuscular blockade
options.why: A boxed warning: caution with paralytics and myasthenia gravis.

options.t: Red man syndrome
options.why: That is vancomycin.

steps.q: Which drugs add to aminoglycoside toxicity?

options.t: Loop diuretics (ototoxicity)
options.why: Furosemide and gentamicin together raise hearing risk.

options.t: Vancomycin, amphotericin B, IV contrast, NSAIDs (kidney)
options.why: Stacking nephrotoxins raises kidney injury.

options.t: Acetaminophen
options.why: Not a meaningful interaction.

cases.pearl: **Big peak, long break. Watch kidneys, ears, and paralytics.**

sources.t: Gentamicin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
Nicolau DP, et al. Experience with a once daily aminoglycoside program (Hartford). Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995;39:650-655

cases.title: Which weight for gentamicin?
cases.stem: A man 5 ft 10 in, actual weight 110 kg, SCr 0.9. Gentamicin extended interval dosing is planned.

steps.q: Calculate his ideal body weight (male: 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 feet).

options.t: 73 kg
110 kg
options.why: That is his actual weight.
That would use the female formula (45.5 base).

steps.q: His actual weight is 151% of ideal. Which weight do you dose on?

options.t: Adjusted body weight: IBW + 0.4 x (actual minus IBW) = 73 + 0.4 x 37 = about 88 kg
options.why: Aminoglycosides stay mostly in body water, and fat holds little water. Most protocols switch to adjusted weight above about 120% of IBW.

options.t: Actual weight, 110 kg
options.why: Overdoses obese patients.

options.t: Ideal weight always
options.why: Underdoses obese patients, since some extra water goes with extra weight.

steps.teach: Know three weights cold: **actual, ideal, adjusted.** Write all three in your note.

steps.q: What is the 7 mg/kg dose?

options.t: About 615 mg (7 x 87.8), rounded per protocol, for example 620 mg
options.why: Round to the nearest 10 or 20 mg per your protocol.

options.t: 770 mg
options.why: That uses actual weight.

cases.pearl: **IBW: 50 (men) or 45.5 (women) + 2.3 per inch over 5 ft. Obese: adjusted = IBW + 0.4 x excess.**

sources.t: Nicolau DP, et al. Experience with a once daily aminoglycoside program (Hartford). Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995;39:650-655

cases.title: Reading the Hartford nomogram
cases.stem: Gentamicin 7 mg/kg was given at 0800. A random level was drawn at 1800.

steps.q: Is the level timing valid for the Hartford nomogram?

options.t: Yes: 10 hours after the start, inside the 6 to 14 hour window
options.why: The nomogram was built for a single level 6 to 14 hours after the start of a 7 mg/kg dose.

options.t: No: the level must be a trough just before the next dose
options.why: Hartford uses one random level, not a trough.

steps.q: The level falls exactly on the line between the q24h and q36h zones. Which interval?

options.t: q36h, the longer interval
options.why: On a line, choose the longer interval. Safer for the kidneys and ears.

options.t: q24h
options.why: On a line you choose the longer interval.

steps.q: Another patient's level is above the q48h zone. What do you do?

options.t: Do not schedule a dose; follow serial levels and redose when the level is below 1 mcg/mL (or switch approach)
options.why: Above the q48h zone means clearance is too slow for this method.

options.t: Give the next dose in 48 hours anyway
options.why: The patient still has too much drug on board.

steps.q: Which patients should NOT be dosed with the Hartford method?

options.t: Pregnancy, burns over 20%, ascites, CrCl below 20 mL/min or dialysis
options.why: These groups were excluded from the original study because their kinetics differ.

options.t: Endocarditis (synergy dosing), cystic fibrosis, children
options.why: Each needs its own regimen.

options.t: A healthy adult with pyelonephritis and normal kidneys
options.why: This is the classic good candidate.

cases.pearl: **7 mg/kg, one level at 6 to 14 h, on a line pick longer. Know the exclusions.**

sources.t: Nicolau DP, et al. Experience with a once daily aminoglycoside program (Hartford). Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995;39:650-655

cases.title: Traditional gentamicin and levels
cases.stem: A patient with unstable kidney function gets traditional gentamicin every 8 hours (30 minute infusion).

steps.q: When are the peak and trough drawn?

options.t: Peak 30 minutes after the end of the 30 minute infusion; trough just before the next dose
options.why: The 30 minute wait after the infusion lets the drug finish distributing.

options.t: Both at random times
options.why: Traditional dosing needs timed peaks and troughs.

steps.q: What are the usual safety limits on the label for traditional dosing?

options.t: Avoid peaks above 12 mcg/mL and troughs above 2 mcg/mL
options.why: Gentamicin label: prolonged concentrations above these raise toxicity.

options.t: Peak above 25 is the goal
options.why: That is above the label safety limit for gentamicin (amikacin uses higher numbers).

steps.q: Levels: 7.0 mcg/mL drawn 1 hour after the start, 1.2 mcg/mL drawn 8 hours after the start. What is the half life?

options.why: Same exponential math as vancomycin.

options.t: About 7 hours
options.why: Recheck: use ln of the ratio over the 7 hours between draws.

cases.pearl: **Traditional: peak 30 min after a 30 min infusion, trough before the next dose. Label limits: peak 12, trough 2.**

cases.title: Gentamicin for synergy in endocarditis
cases.stem: Enterococcus faecalis endocarditis. The ID team wants ampicillin plus gentamicin.

steps.q: How is synergy dosing different from gram negative dosing?

options.t: Lower doses: about 3 mg/kg per day in divided doses (for example 1 mg/kg every 8 hours), targeting a peak of 3 to 4 and a trough below 1
options.why: For synergy, gentamicin helps the cell wall drug kill; you do not need high gram negative peaks (AHA 2015).

options.t: 7 mg/kg once daily by Hartford
options.why: Hartford is not for endocarditis synergy.

steps.q: What alternative avoids aminoglycoside toxicity for E. faecalis endocarditis?

options.t: Ampicillin plus ceftriaxone (double beta lactam)
options.why: AHA 2015 lists it as a reasonable option, especially with kidney risk or high level aminoglycoside resistance.

options.t: Vancomycin alone
options.why: Not preferred for susceptible E. faecalis.

cases.pearl: **Synergy gent: about 1 mg/kg every 8 h, peak 3 to 4, trough below 1. Or ampicillin + ceftriaxone.**

sources.t: Baddour LM, et al. Infective endocarditis in adults (AHA 2015). Circulation 2015;132:1435-1486

cases.title: The patient who says "my ears are ringing"
cases.stem: Day 9 of gentamicin for a complicated urinary infection. The patient reports ringing in the ears and feels unsteady walking. She is also on IV furosemide.

steps.q: What is the concern?

options.t: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity (cochlear and vestibular), made more likely by the long course and the loop diuretic
options.why: Ototoxicity is often irreversible, so early action matters.

options.t: Normal side effect, continue
options.why: Never ignore ear symptoms on an aminoglycoside.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Tell the team today; ask whether gentamicin can be stopped or switched based on cultures (for example to a beta lactam)
options.why: Most urinary gram negatives have options with less toxicity.

options.t: Check levels and kidney function, and review the need for furosemide
options.why: High troughs and stacked ototoxins raise risk.

options.t: Suggest an audiology evaluation
options.why: Documents the baseline of damage.

cases.pearl: **Ringing or dizziness on gent = call today. Ear damage may not come back.**

sources.t: Gentamicin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)

cases.title: Shift simulation: three kinetics calls
cases.stem: Three things land together: (1) a septic ICU patient needs a vancomycin load and no dose is ordered yet; (2) a gentamicin random level came back for a stable pyelonephritis patient; (3) a vancomycin AUC from yesterday reads 455 on a stable patient.

steps.q: What do you do first?

options.t: Get the septic patient's vancomycin loading dose ordered and sent
options.why: Time to effective antibiotics drives survival in septic shock.

options.t: Plot the gentamicin level
options.why: Important, but the next dose is hours away.

options.t: Document the AUC of 455
options.why: On target; it can wait.

steps.q: Second?

options.t: Plot the gentamicin level and set the next dose time
options.why: The next dose time depends on the level.

options.t: The AUC note
options.why: Routine.

steps.q: For the septic patient (90 kg), what loading dose fits?

options.t: 2,000 to 2,250 mg (about 22 to 25 mg/kg), infused per policy
options.why: Inside 20 to 35 mg/kg and under the 3,000 mg cap.

options.t: 1,000 mg because she might have kidney problems
options.why: Loads are not reduced for kidney function.

cases.pearl: **Septic first dose, then level driven next doses, then documentation.**
